metrics.name: Complexity
metrics.description: Cyclomatic complexity (McCabe score) — how many independent execution paths exist in each function.

summaries.red: High complexity detected (max %1). Functions are hard to test.

metrics.finding_template: Cyclomatic complexity %1 — consider splitting this function.
metrics.help_text: Cyclomatic complexity counts the number of independent paths through a function. CC of 1 means one straight path. Each if/for/while/case adds 1. High CC means the function is hard to test and easy to have bugs in. Target: CC < 10 per function.

metrics.name: Readability
metrics.description: Function length, nesting depth, parameter counts, and single-letter variable names.

checks.title: Function too long
checks.help_text: Long functions are harder to understand and test. Aim for functions that do one thing and fit on one screen (30 lines or less).

checks.title: Too many parameters
checks.detail_template: %1 parameters (recommended max 5). Consider grouping into a struct/object.
checks.help_text: Functions with many parameters are hard to call correctly and easy to misuse. Group related parameters into a struct or class.

checks.title: Deep nesting
checks.detail_template: Maximum nesting depth %1 (recommended max 4). Consider early returns.
checks.help_text: Deeply nested code is hard to read. Use early returns (guard clauses) to reduce nesting.

checks.title: Single-letter variable name
checks.detail: Single-letter variable name makes code harder to understand.
checks.help_text: Variable names should describe what they hold. Single letters (except loop counters i/j/k) make code unreadable.

summaries.green: Code is easy to read. Good function lengths and clear structure.
summaries.yellow: Some readability issues — long functions or deep nesting detected.
summaries.red: Serious readability issues. Functions are too long or too deeply nested.

metrics.name: Duplication

summaries.yellow: Some duplicated code blocks — consider extracting a shared function.
summaries.red: Significant duplication detected. Duplicated code is harder to maintain.

metrics.finding_template: Block of ~%1 lines appears %2 times (first at line %3).
metrics.help_text: Duplicated code means bugs must be fixed in multiple places. Extract repeated code into a function and call it from all the places that need it.

metrics.name: Dead Code
metrics.description: Variables defined but never read, and functions defined but never called.

checks.title: Unused variable
checks.detail_template: '%1' is assigned but never read after line %2.
checks.help_text: Unused variables clutter the code and confuse readers. Remove them or rename with _ prefix if intentionally ignored.

checks.title: Unused function
checks.help_text: Unused functions add dead weight to the codebase. Remove them or check if they should be called but aren't.

summaries.yellow: Some unused variables or functions detected.
summaries.red: Multiple dead code items found. Clean up unused variables and functions.

metrics.name: Naming
metrics.description: Whether identifiers follow accepted conventions for the language.

checks.title: Function name should be snake_case
checks.detail_template: '%1' looks like camelCase or PascalCase — Python convention is snake_case.
checks.help_text: Python functions should use snake_case (words separated by underscores). E.g., calculate_total not calculateTotal.

checks.title: Class name should be PascalCase
checks.detail_template: '%1' starts with lowercase — Python class convention is PascalCase.
checks.help_text: Python classes should use PascalCase (each word starts with uppercase). E.g., DataProcessor not data_processor.

summaries.green: Names follow conventions for this language.
summaries.red: Multiple naming convention violations. Consistent naming improves readability.
